chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khazzāz, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from Abū Isḥāq, from Jābir, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Judhāʿah, who said:
I asked him about four persons who testified against two men and two women for zina. He said: “They are to be stoned.”

key_terms.بِالزِّنَى: for zina, meaning unlawful sexual intercourse
key_terms.رَجُلَيْنِ: two men accused in the case
key_terms.شَهِدُوا: they gave testimony or bore witness in a legal case
key_terms.وَامْرَأَتَيْنِ: and two women accused in the case
key_terms.يُرْجَمُونَ: they are to be punished by stoning

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when four witnesses testify against two men and two women for zina?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling concerning testimony in a zina case involving two men and two women. The Imam عليه السلام states that the ruling is rajm, indicating a juridical judgment within the law of prescribed punishments.
